implementerProof.how: Ran the implementer's commands again at 2ba3ba48 on this pod's Postgres 17. The multiprocess package passed (688.3 s). The outbox (242.6 s; the round's new tests TestOneBrokenRowOfARecipientReadCostsTheBatchAboutTwoStatementsPerHalving, TestABrokenRowOfAnEventThatIsNotDueFailsNoOtherOwnersRecipientRead, TestAnEventBehindAnotherThatIsNotDueIsHeldOnlyOnTheKeysTheOtherCouldStillOwe and TestARefusedConnectionOrAFailingServerIsNoRefusedStatement among them), deliveryaudit, duty, bus and cmd/listener packages all passed. I drove review finding 1 on real processes, against the previous head as the negative control (proof below).

proof.criterion: Review finding 1: an event waiting out a back-off holds a later event of its issue back only on the keys it could still owe, not from a session it already reached
proof.surface: two real envoy-dispatch binaries (multiprocess harness, throwaway probe TestProbeNotDueEventHoldsOnlyItsStalledKey). Issue X is routed to a role whose holder H withholds its receipt. Thread A: root by T1, reply by T2. Thread B: root by T2. A person's reply N in thread A reaches T1 and, through thread A's recipient read, T2; its role forward to H gets no receipt, so N is backed off and not due. A person's reply N+1 in thread B, which T2 rooted, is then written
proof.command: cd packages/envoy (scratch copy) && GOWORK=off DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<pg> go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -run TestProbeNotDueEventHoldsOnlyItsStalledKey -v ./cmd/dispatch, at 2ba3ba48 and at 2f3bf214
proof.observed: At 2ba3ba48, N+1 reached T2 21 ms after its write while N (attempts 3) waited on H. Once H answered, H took N and then N+1. Every session's frames were in order
proof.negativeControl: At 2f3bf214 (the previous head), N+1 reached T2 only 3.973 s after its write, held until N's retry, although N had already reached T2. The probe fails there with 'N+1 waited 3.972836316s for T2, a key N already reached'. That is the defect the review found
